images.title: Copy the angle, get parallel
images.purpose: Show a second line drawn at the same 60 degree angle to the transversal, giving parallel lines.
images.composition: Two lines and a transversal centred on the canvas, with the two equal angles clearly marked and space around.
exact_structure: Line l: horizontal teal (#0072B2) line, upper; line m: horizontal amber (#E69F00) line, lower, equal length.
Transversal t: slanting dark line crossing l at point X and m at point Y; t rises to the right, so the angle between t and the right half of each line, above the line, is 60°.
Angle a at X is the upper right angle between t and l, filled reddish purple (#CC79A7), labelled 60°.
Angle b at Y is the upper right angle between t and m, filled reddish purple (#CC79A7), labelled 60°.
Two small arrow marks (>>) drawn on the middle of l and of m show they are parallel.
Points X and Y are small dots on t.
rejection: angle a and angle b not both 60°
the two filled angles in different corners
images.takeaway: Equal corresponding angles of 60° make the two lines parallel.
images.description: Lines l and m crossed by t, with the matching 60° angles a and b marked and arrow marks showing parallel.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students compare a and b and see the second line has the same slant as the first.

image_decisions.why: Drawing the same angle at Y is the way to draw a parallel line.
